Conocimiento del negocio : Comprender las dinámicas comerciales, indicadores de ventas, precios, portafolio, clientes y comportamiento del mercado, integrando el contexto de negocio en los análisis para generar recomendaciones de valor y apoyar una mejor toma de decisiones. Comunicación ejecutiva : Traducir análisis complejos en mensajes claros, estructurados y orientados a la toma de decisiones, desarrollando presentaciones ejecutivas de alto impacto para Dirección, Vicepresidencia y distintos foros ejecutivos. Proactividad : Anticiparse a las necesidades de información del negocio, identificando oportunidades, riesgos, tendencias y análisis de valor antes de que sean solicitados, generando recomendaciones que faciliten la toma de decisiones. Manejo experto de bases, modelos, fórmulas, tablas dinámicas, Power Query, automatización y estructuración de reportes. Power BI: Indispensable. Creación de tableros, modelado, visualización y publicación de indicadores. PowerPoint / storytelling ejecutivo: Importante. Capacidad de presentar hallazgos de forma ejecutiva y clara. Python: Deseable. Automatización, limpieza, transformación y análisis de datos. SQL / bases de datos: Deseable. Consulta, cruce y estructuración de información. Snowflake: Deseable. Manejo o entendimiento de entornos modernos de datos. Inglés: Nivel intermedio Relaciones Relaciones Director Comercial: Usuario principal de información, análisis e insights ejecutivos. Gerentes Comerciales: Solicitudes de análisis, seguimiento a resultados, explicación de variaciones y oportunidades. Asesores Comerciales: Entrega de información comercial accionable para gestión con clientes. Jefaturas de información / analistas pares: Homologación de criterios, colaboración, mejores prácticas y continuidad operativa. GES / Planeación / Cadena de Suministro/ Otras: Compartir información que permita la gestión de cada una de las áreas. Clientes / distribuidores: Podría existir interacción puntual cuando se requiera contexto comercial o aclaración específica. Proveedores de herramientas / soporte tecnológico: Interacción eventual para resolver temas técnicos o de automatización. Respetamos la diversidad, abordamos la inclusión y la no-discriminación de cualquier persona con talento, independientemente de su género, capacidad física, edad, orientación sexual, cultura, origen étnico, religión, afiliación política, estado civil, embarazo/maternidad/paternidad y nacionalidad. Description: Job Description Engineering Guadalajara, hybrid 6 Months Fixed Term, Transitioning to Permanent Learn to build with AI. Own what ships. Grow into a great engineer. This is the start of your career, and we want it to count. If you’re early in your software engineering journey and you want to get good fast, working in an experienced team that builds with AI, SPAN is for you. It's also your entry point into SPAN LEAP (Learn, Engineer, Apply, Progress) our structured development program built to turn early-career engineers into well-rounded, AI-ready engineers. You'll not only write code but learn to think like an engineer, breaking problems down, directing AI toward clear, testable goals, and knowing when a solution, yours or the AI's, is right. You'll ship real, live work from day one, backed by a team who've done this before, building the judgment and habits that separate the engineers who thrive from the ones who plateau. We're looking for people who think critically, stay curious, and adapt fast when things change. About SPAN LEAP This role sits inside SPAN LEAP, our 12-month track that develops early-career engineers into AI-ready software engineers through real work rather than classroom training. The program runs in two stages: Stage 1: the first 6 months are a fixed-term training and evaluation period, during which we assess fit and progress against the program’s plan. Stage 2: Engineers who are meeting expectations may then continue the remaining 6 months of LEAP with the same mentorship and structured growth, but as permanent SPAN employees - a status that continues beyond the program's completion. As a SPAN LEAP Participant, You Can Expect A structured path across core engineering skill areas: front-end, APIs, data, DevOps, testing, documentation, with AI readiness built in from day one, not bolted on afterward. A real mentorship model: a working SPAN engineer is paired with you and spends dedicated time every week guiding you on live projects, alongside pair programming and structured, group-based learning loops with the rest of your cohort. Hands-on AI engineering practice: learning to direct and orchestrate AI tools toward well-defined, testable goals, not just use them as a shortcut. What You'll Do As an associate engineer, you'll work as part of a delivery team, taking on small, well-defined pieces of work with support from senior engineers. Day to day, you'll: Write, review, reason about, and validate code for small, clearly defined features, making sure it meets our coding standards and practices. Use AI tools and help orchestrate AI agents toward well-defined, testable goals. Investigate and fix bugs with guidance from more experienced engineers. Write and run tests, and make sure coverage handles both the basic cases and the edge cases. Take part in code reviews as both an author and a reviewer, and act on the feedback you get. Help configure and maintain the automated quality gates that keep our code healthy, and understand why those standards exist. Own the quality of your output, regardless of how it was produced. What We're Looking For You don't need years of experience. You do need a real foundation, strong critical thinking, and the drive to build on both. We're looking for someone who: Has 6-12 months experience. Can read and write code in at least one programming language (Java, Python, or Golang, TypeScript preferred), and understands core software development concepts. Breaks problems down clearly and can reason about whether a solution really is correct. Is keen to work with AI coding tools, and understands that the engineer owns the result, not the tool. Is comfortable with version control, or eager to learn Git properly. Learns quickly, asks substantive questions, and treats feedback as a way to get better. Communicates clearly and works well as part of a team. Nice to have None of these are required. Any of them will help you stand out: Hands-on experience with AI development tools, such as AI coding assistants or agent-based workflows. A portfolio, GitHub profile, or personal projects we can look at. Exposure to testing, a web or mobile framework, or a cloud platform. Internship, freelance, or open-source experience. How You'll Grow Growth is built into how we work, not left to chance. As a LEAP participant, you'll follow a personal growth plan over the 12-month program with clear goals, paired with a dedicated mentor. You'll learn through pair programming with senior engineers, AI-assisted learning loops, code review, and career coaching, and we'll measure your progress against SFIA, the globally recognized skills framework we use across the company. The expectation is simple: take more on, with less supervision, as your skills and judgment develop. Performance during the first 6 months determines whether you continue in the program as a permanent SPAN employee for the remaining 6 months, with growth and SFIA-based progression continuing through the full 12-month arc - after which you remain a permanent SPAN employee with LEAP complete. Senior people take real accountability for outcomes, document what they build, and hand it off well. Our Product teams draw on that same vantage point to build software that helps enterprises capture and use their own knowledge and gives engineering leaders real-time visibility into the systems they run, so they can make faster, more consistent decisions. We're a global, high-performing team building smart solutions for ambitious clients.
